title: Monument Valley and Rifle: Monitoring Plant-Based Approaches to Milling Site Remediation
summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency estimates there are as many as 15,000 sites associated with abandoned uranium mine (AUM) waste across the American West. The Navajo Nation alone is affected by more than 500 of them. Most of this material has sat on the surface for more than half a century—on federal land, state land, private land, and tribal land—weathering into soil and water while the communities nearest to it wait.

title: NRC issues final rule on ACRS reform
summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has finalized a rule impacting the role of the agency’s independent Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards. The direct final rule streamlines the ACRS’s role in reviews, focusing its work solely on safety-significant issues that are considered novel or noteworthy. The rulemaking defines novel or noteworthy as attributes of a “facility’s design, siting, and operation associated with 1) safety-related structures, systems, and components as described by the definitions given in NRC rules and regulations or 2) structures, systems, and components that perform safety-significant functions.”

title: France’s State Auditor Warns On Funding Problems For Six Planned EPR2 Nuclear Power Plants
summary: French state utility and nuclear plant operator EDF could face difficulties funding the construction of six new generation nuclear reactors, a state auditor’s report said ​on 16 November. In a report on public support for energy (French only), the Cour des Comptes, France’s public audit body, said the utility faces heavy financial exposure across its long-term nuclear projects and could ​require substantial state backing if energy market revenues fail to ​cover building, maintenance and operating costs. It said EDF’s planned construction of ⁠six EPR2 reactors is budgeted at €72.8bn ($80.24bn) in 2020 values, ​which the court calculated at €84bn in 2025 values, with first ​commercial operation scheduled from 2038.

title: Going critical in Phoenix: ANS Winter Conference opens with a call for durability
summary: A week that brought down the country’s email and grounded its airplanes could not stop the nuclear community from getting together in Phoenix. title: Landowner and Community Communications to the PJM Board Concerning RTEP Projects
Newcleo And Curio Announce Collaboration To Advance Recycled Nuclear Fuel Supply
summary: France-based advanced nuclear technology company Newcleo and Curio Legacy Ventures, a Washington-based company developing its patented NuCycle used nuclear fuel recycling process, announced an agreement to collaborate on the supply of recycled used nuclear fuel and transuranic materials for the production of mixed-oxide (MOX) fuel at Newcleo’s planned US fuel manufacturing facility. The fuel would be used in Newcleo’s lead-cooled fast reactors (LFRs) once they are deployed. A statement said that by combining Curio’s advanced nuclear fuel recycling technology with Newcleo’s MOX fuel fabrication capabilities and LFRs, the companies aim to maximise the reuse of nuclear materials, reduce reliance on fresh uranium resources and minimise long-lived radioactive waste.
